describe.estimator: Each hit is one observation and these columns are unweighted. count, mean, min and max are exact; the quartiles are exact too (linear interpolation between order statistics, the pandas describe() convention); sd is the unbiased sample estimator (ddof = 1) and sd_population the ddof = 0 form. No standard error of a mean is quoted: the hits of one shower are strongly correlated, so a hit count would claim a precision the events do not have.
describe.weighting_note: The ew columns weight every hit by its deposited energy. ew_mean = Σ E·a / Σ E exactly; the ew quartiles are read off 1 mm histograms of the weighted coordinate (0.01-decade bins of log10 E for the energy row) and are exact to one bin. They say where the energy sits, not where the hits are: a different weighting, not a correction of the unweighted columns.

intervals.hits_fraction: 95% Student-t, ratio of sums, events as clusters
intervals.energy_fraction: 95% Student-t, ratio of sums, events as clusters
intervals.showers_with_any: 95% Wilson score, showers (one per event only)

negative_w.summary: w < −10⁻⁶ mm: 7.12% [6.00, 8.23] of energy, 24.04% [21.43, 26.66] of hits; 49.8% [44.1, 55.6] of showers (95% intervals in brackets)

notes: u, v, w are each hit's position in its own shower's frame, w along the incident direction from the entry point P0, so w < 0 lies upstream of it (see the negative-depth block). ρ = √(u² + v²) is the 2-D transverse radius from the shower axis, the reference notebook's r_local; core.py's r_local is the 3-D distance and is not this quantity.

A hit is at negative depth when w = z_local < −10⁻⁶ mm in its own shower's frame, whatever frame the other numbers are drawn in. The counts come from the event table, so they are exact even on a preview. Energies are the raw deposited hit energies (GeV), not calibrated to the incident momentum; a share of them is unaffected by the calibration.

The hits of one shower share its development, and the two showers of an event share the event, so every fraction takes events as its sampling unit: a ratio of sums with the linearised cluster standard error and a Student-t interval, clipped to [0, 1].

The share of events with any such hit is a proportion and takes a Wilson score interval. The share of showers is given only where each event contributes one shower: the two showers of an event are not independent Bernoulli trials.
